Aromanian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • porcu

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin porcus. Compare Romanian porc.

Noun

[edit]

porc m (plural ports)

  1. pig

Related terms

[edit]
  • porche
  • purtsel, purtsiau
  • purcar

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Catalan porc, from Latin porcus, from Proto-Italic *porkos, from Proto-Indo-European *pórḱos (“young swine, young pig”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [ˈpɔrk]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈpɔɾk]
  • Audio (Valencia):(file)

Noun

[edit]

porc m (plural porcs)

  1. pig, swine
  2. pork
    Synonym: carn de porc

Derived terms

[edit]
  • porc senglar

Related terms

[edit]
  • porcell
  • porquer
  • porquerol

References

[edit]
  • “porc”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007
  • “porc”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026
  • “porc” in Diccionari normatiu valencià, Acadèmia Valenciana de la Llengua.
  • “porc” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle French porc, from Old French porc, from Latin porcus, from Proto-Italic *porkos, from Proto-Indo-European *pórḱos (“young swine, young pig”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pɔʁ/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Paris):(file)
  • Audio (France (Saint-Maurice-de-Beynost)):(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Agen)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)
  • Homophones: porcs, port, ports

Noun

[edit]

porc m (plural porcs)

  1. pork
  2. pig
    Synonym: cochon
  3. (slang, vulgar, derogatory, offensive) dirty pig, swine, contemptible person
    sale porc! ― dirty pig!
  4. (chiefly Quebec, slang, derogatory, usually in the plural) pig; cop
    Synonyms: see Thesaurus:policier

Usage notes

[edit]
  • Used as an insult, the word porc is rather harsh or even dirty (especially with epithets such as "sale" or "gros") whereas the word cochon in the same sense has a more affectionate or childish meaning. Thus, "mon petit cochon" could be translate as "you little dirty one ", using porc instead of cochon is here very unusual or may be viewed as an awkward dirty talking line.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • balancer son porc

Related terms

[edit]
  • porcher
  • pourceau

Further reading

[edit]
  • “porc”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Hungarian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Back-formation from porcogó (“cartilage”). Created during the Hungarian language reform, which took place in the 18th–19th centuries.[1]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈport͡s]
  • Hyphenation: porc
  • Rhymes: -ort͡s

Noun

[edit]

porc (plural porcok)

  1. gristle
  2. (anatomy) cartilage

Old French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin porcus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpɔɾk/

Noun

[edit]

porc oblique singular, m (oblique plural pors, nominative singular pors, nominative plural porc)

  1. pig; hog; swine
    • 1377, Bernard de Gordon, Fleur de lis de medecine (a.k.a. lilium medicine), page 180 of this essay:
      il ne doit mengier […] chair de porc
      he must not eat […] pork (literally, the flesh of a pig)

Synonyms

[edit]
  • bacon

Descendants

[edit]
  • Middle French: porc
    • French: porc
  • Norman: por
  • → Middle English: pork, porc, porke
    • English: pork
    • Scots: pork, porc, porck

Noun

porc m (oblique plural porcs, nominative singular porcs, nominative plural porc)

  1. pig (mammal)

Descendants

[edit]
  • Occitan: pòrc

References

[edit]
  • Walther von Wartburg (1928–2002), “porcus”, in Französisches Etymologisches Wörterbuch, volume 9: Placabilis–Pyxis, page 189

  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

porc m (plural porci)

  1. pig (mammal of genus Sus), hog, swine
  2. pork

singular plural
